title: Translation-Induced Circuit Bypass: Safety Circuits Found in English Fail to Generalize to Other Languages

original_idea.quick_reasoning: Clearly addresses an AI Safety problem with a reasonably scoped approach.

theory_of_impact.reasoning: Multilingual jailbreaks are a documented attack class. If safety circuits are language-specific, English-only interpretability audits provide no guarantees for global deployment. Clear and direct safety implication.

accessible_complexity.reasoning: Activation patching on a multilingual model is feasible with TransformerLens. Generating equivalent prompts in multiple languages is straightforward. Requires a multilingual model but several are available (mGPT, BLOOM-small).

narrow_scope.reasoning: Clear deliverable: circuit activation rates across languages. Testing 3-4 languages keeps scope manageable. Correlating with jailbreak success rates adds scope but is a natural extension. Core experiment is tight.

novelty.reasoning: This is heavily studied territory. (1) 'A Cross-Language Investigation into Jailbreak Attacks in LLMs' (arXiv:2401.16765, ICLR 2024) demonstrates multilingual jailbreaking with interpretability analysis. (2) 'Multilingual Jailbreak Challenges in LLMs' (ICLR 2024) shows low-resource languages have 3x the harmful content likelihood. (3) Critically, 'Refusal Direction is Universal Across Safety-Aligned Languages' (arXiv:2505.17306, 2025) directly addresses safety circuits cross-lingually, finding that refusal vectors extracted from English transfer to other languages with near-perfect effectiveness — meaning safety circuits ARE somewhat shared, partially contradicting the premise. (4) 'English as Defense Proxy' (2025) proposes using English safety knowledge as a universal anchor. The cross-lingual safety gap is well-documented and the mechanistic interpretability angle on refusal directions has been specifically studied.
